title: Brotherly closeness and Pat as trailblazer
summary: The brothers never argue; Pat led the way, got John onto Buddy Rich's band, and still advises him on tunes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Jumping back to our how we started, and I believe Pat told me that you guys never argued.
If I got all of you on a four-person Zoom could I think of something that might make you argue together?

Not really. We’re pretty much on the same page. It was our upbringing, that Sicilian upbringing, the family is very close. But of course we’re all in the same business and we all came up together listening to the same stuff, and we have similar political opinions and societal opinions. We talk every week if not more. And as I get closer to my next recording we’ll be talking even more than that. But no we never argue. I mean we would punch each other or hit each other when we were kids, little kids, but no, we don’t argue at all.
As your careers were expanding did you ever get on the phone with them for advice about a decision you needed to make?

Yeah, especially with Pat, ‘cause Pat was the one who led us all. Pat was out there first. He was the trailblazer. You know I’m the middle, well-adjusted son. But he was the one who took all the blows. He’s the one who got me on Buddy Rich’s band you know. He, you know he would, I’d call him for some advice. Yup. And he’s so knowledgeable. I’ll

still call him about certain changes. I’ll say, on this tune, actually I just did that recently ‘cause we’re doing a tune that he did with Elvin Jones. I’m doing it on my next recording. And I would call him and say what the hell is this, what is all this stuff. And of course he’s got it all in his head. He’s got all these tunes. And he would give me some ideas. Because not everything is consistent in, even in modal writing, nothing is that consistent and there’s always something new to bridge, something new to discover. And when I hear something like that I’ll call Pat and say what did he do here, what is that, if I can’t figure it out myself.
